national_raw_news.content: The government has announced that banks cannot impose any charges on Unified Payments Interface (UPI) transactions of up to 2,000 rupees. According to a government gazette notification no charges can be imposed on such 2,000 rupees payments made through RuPay-powered debit cards either. The notification said no bank or system provider can impose any direct or indirect charge on a person making or receiving payments through these modes. The Finance Ministry notified the changes under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act to clarify the rules around charges on UPI transactions. The notification specifically categorised RuPay-powered debit cards and UPI transactions of up to 2,000 rupees as “electronic modes of payment”. Last month, the government clarified that consumers will not be charged for making payments through the Unified Payments Interface (UPI), while any future merchant discount rate (MDR) will be limited to select transactions above a specified threshold. The Finance Ministry said that all person-to-person (P2P) UPI transactions will continue to remain free and there will be no blanket MDR on merchants. The government further added that such charges would be significantly lower than the MDR applicable to debit or credit card transactions. The clarification comes amid debate over a recent amendment to the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007, with concerns being raised about the possibility of charges being imposed on UPI users.

national_raw_news.title: 54 mins ago | National 32 World Circular Economy Forum 2026 to begin today at Gandhinagar in Gujarat
national_raw_news.content: The prestigious ‘World Circular Economy Forum (WCEF) 2026’ is set to begin today at Mahatma Mandir in Gandhinagar, Gujarat. The conference which is being held for the first time in South Asia, will be jointly inaugurated by Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change Bhupender Yadav and Gujarat Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel. Held under the theme ‘Circular Economy: Transition for People and Prosperity,’ the event will gather over 2,000 stakeholders from more than 65 countries. The stage is set at Mahatma Mandir in Gandhinagar for the World Circular Economy Forum 2026, marking a major milestone in promoting sustainable economic transitions across South Asia. The forum aims to drive global circularity by emphasising the reuse, refurbishing, and recycling of materials to reintegrate them as valuable economic resources. Across the two days, the forum will host 4 plenary sessions and 16 thematic sessions covering key areas such as the application of AI, green energy, sustainable finance, governance, and the start-up ecosystem. Additionally, an international expo featuring over 125 exhibitors will showcase innovative, practical solutions for circular business models. The global event is jointly organised by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Central Pollution Control Board, Finnish Innovation Fund Sitra, and the Government of Gujarat. Union Minister of State for Environment Kirti Vardhan Singh and Finland’s Environment Minister Sari Multala will grace the valedictory session tomorrow, which will be followed by 80 accelerator sessions hosted globally on September 17th and 18th.

national_raw_news.title: 56 mins ago | National 39 CJI Surya Kant calls mechanism to address complaints against judges robust and timely
national_raw_news.content: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant has described the mechanism developed by the Supreme Court and high courts to address complaints against judges as robust, very responsive and timely, while stressing the need for continuous reform and greater transparency in the judiciary. Delivering the keynote address at the 6th Ram Jethmalani Memorial Lecture on Justice Seen to Be Done: Transparency and Public Trust as Pillars of the Legal System, in New Delhi yesterday, the CJI said reform must remain the norm and no institution could afford to take pride in remaining static. He said the judiciary itself had acknowledged the importance of criticism, reiterating the Supreme Court’s position that the institution is not, and cannot be, averse to criticism. He added fair, informed and constructive critique of judicial functioning is a legitimate and necessary feature of a vibrant constitutional democracy. Justice Surya Kant said this principle was at the heart of judicial transparency. He observed a court, cannot expect to command public confidence by placing itself beyond scrutiny. Instead, it must remain open to being examined, questioned and, where necessary, criticised. He also drew a distinction between public trust and public approval, saying true public trust is established when even those who lose a case continue to believe that the judicial process was fair.
